title: Amazon Bar Raiser & Tier-1 Behavioral Evaluation Rubric

competencies.name: Customer Obsession
positive_signals: Advocated for customer experience despite internal technical inertia or friction.
Refused to launch a flawed product to hit an artificial internal deadline.
Dug into telemetry metrics to understand unvoiced customer pain.
negative_signals: Prioritized internal engineering vanity projects over real customer bugs.
Dismissed user confusion as user error.

competencies.name: Ownership
positive_signals: Stepped up outside direct ticket scope to prevent a production failure.
Took full responsibility for a mistake without shifting blame to teammates or juniors.
Built lasting documentation and automated tests for future engineers.
negative_signals: Said 'that's not my job' or blamed product management.
Left temporary hacks in production without a remediation ticket.

competencies.name: Bias for Action
positive_signals: Made calculated, high-velocity technical decisions under incomplete data.
Implemented rollback strategies and feature flags to manage deployment risk.
Chose iterative deployment over endless architecture paralysis.
negative_signals: Waited for committee consensus before fixing an active customer problem.
Over-engineered simple features for hypothetical future requirements.

competencies.name: Dive Deep
positive_signals: Analyzed database execution plans, kernel logs, and network packet traces personally.
Refused to accept surface symptom explanations for intermittent failures.
Understood the root cause and implemented preventive architectural controls.
negative_signals: Rebooted servers to resolve memory leaks without capturing core dumps.
Relied purely on teammate opinions without verifying data.
